browserhive/axtree-shape.collapsed-role: line {line}: roles that should have been collapsed are still in the tree ({roles})
browserhive/axtree-shape.desc: browserhive: checks the recorded accessibility tree against the pruning rules the BrowserHive WACZ Profile declares
browserhive/axtree-shape.not-json: {entry} line {line} is not a JSON object
browserhive/axtree-shape.unknown-propert: line {line}: nodes carry properties the BrowserHive WACZ Profile does not allow ({keys})
browserhive/behaviors-shape.desc: browserhive: checks the contents of behaviors/custom.jsonl against settings.behaviors. Every behavior the settings report as coming from the request must have its source here — that source arrived with the request and is recoverable from nowhere else once the response is discarded. The converse is not required: a line may have no matching entry, because a behavior can be placed in the page and then decline to act, and the code still ran.
browserhive/behaviors-shape.missing-entr: settings.behaviors reports {id} as request-supplied, but behaviors/custom.jsonl is absent
browserhive/behaviors-shape.missing-memb: behaviors/custom.jsonl line {line} is missing {members} (required by BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.5.0)
browserhive/behaviors-shape.not-json: behaviors/custom.jsonl line {line} is not a JSON object
browserhive/behaviors-shape.source-missi: settings.behaviors reports {id} as request-supplied, but behaviors/custom.jsonl has no line for it
browserhive/behaviors-shape.unknown-prof: behaviors/custom.jsonl line {line} declares profile {found}, which this version does not define
browserhive/dismissal-shape.desc: browserhive: checks the shape of browserhive:capture.dismissal when it is present. It must carry the selectors and heuristic that were in force even when nothing was removed — an empty list of removals reads the same whether twenty selectors were tried or none, so the outcome is only checkable next to the input. And a removal that could not be carried out must state that instead of reporting an empty result, because it observed nothing.
browserhive/dismissal-shape.missing-memb: dismissal is missing {member} (required by BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.4.0 whenever dismissal is present)
browserhive/dismissal-shape.not-object: browserhive:capture.dismissal is {found}, expected a JSON object
browserhive/dismissal-shape.unreadable-w: dismissal carries unreadable alongside {members} — a removal that could not be carried out has observed nothing, so it must not also state a result
browserhive/dismissal-shape.wrong-type: dismissal.{member} is {found}, which is not the type BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.4.0 defines
browserhive/settings-shape.desc: browserhive: checks that browserhive:capture.settings carries every member the BrowserHive WACZ Profile requires. Without this check a producer can drop a required member and still claim conformance — which is how the cache member stayed in 1.1.0 for several releases after no implementation wrote it.
browserhive/settings-shape.missing: browserhive:capture.settings is missing (required by the BrowserHive WACZ Profile)
browserhive/settings-shape.missing-membe: settings is missing {member} (required by the BrowserHive WACZ Profile)
browserhive/settings-shape.wrong-type: settings.{member} is {found}, which is not the type the BrowserHive WACZ Profile defines
browserhive/settings-shape.secret-archiv: settings.secretArchive names {name}, which is not in settings.secrets
settings.secretArchive.{name} is not keep, the only value the BrowserHive WACZ Profile defines
browserhive/user-agent-recorded.desc: browserhive: every request record for mainPageURL carries settings.userAgent in its User-Agent header (BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.20.0). Without this check, settings can name a value the capture never sent.
browserhive/user-agent-recorded.mismatch: {url}: the request record sent User-Agent "{sent}", but settings.userAgent says "{recorded}"
browserhive/user-agent-recorded.absent: {url}: the request record has no User-Agent header, but settings.userAgent says "{recorded}"
browserhive/settle-deadline.desc: browserhive: reports an archive whose wait after navigation ran into its deadline, naming the signals that were not satisfied. This is not a violation — BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.7.0 says a deadline is not a failure, and the package holds what the page had become by then. It is shown because a reader weighing the archive as evidence needs to know the page was still changing when it was taken, and nothing else in the archive says so.
browserhive/settle-deadline.still-changi: the page had not settled when it was captured: {signals} not satisfied by the deadline (waited {waitedMs} ms of {maxMs} ms)
browserhive/settle-shape.deadline-withou: settle.endedBy is "deadline" but every signal has a time — a wait that met every signal ended quiet
browserhive/settle-shape.desc: browserhive: checks browserhive:capture.settle against BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.7.0. It must be present, since the wait runs on every capture. Every signal's time must be written, as null when the signal was not satisfied: an omitted time reads as a signal nobody watched. And endedBy must agree with the times — "quiet" beside a null, or "deadline" with none, is a claim the capture did not earn.
browserhive/settle-shape.missing: browserhive:capture.settle is missing (required by BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.7.0)
browserhive/settle-shape.missing-member: settle is missing {member} (required by BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.7.0)
browserhive/settle-shape.missing-time: settle.{member} is absent — a signal that was not satisfied is written as null, and an absent time reads as a signal that was not watched
browserhive/settle-shape.not-object: browserhive:capture.settle is {found}, expected a JSON object
browserhive/settle-shape.quiet-with-null: settle.endedBy is "quiet" but {signals} not satisfied — a wait that missed a signal ended on its deadline
browserhive/settle-shape.unknown-strateg: settle.strategy is {found}; BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.7.0 defines only {expected}
browserhive/settle-shape.wrong-type: settle.{member} is {found}, which is not the type BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.7.0 defines
browserhive/storage-inventory.desc: browserhive: checks that the archive records what web storage the captured origins held. The inventory is required by BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.1.0: without it a reader cannot tell a page that rendered from localStorage from one that had nothing to show, and completeness cannot say so because storage never became a body.
browserhive/storage-inventory.digest-sha: {where}.digest is {found}, expected sha256: followed by 64 lowercase hex digits
browserhive/storage-inventory.missing: browserhive:capture.storage is missing (required by BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.1.0)
browserhive/storage-inventory.origin-for: {where} must carry either both areas or unreadable: true — an origin that was empty and one that could not be read are different claims
browserhive/storage-inventory.oversize-s: {where}.valuesOversize is {found}, expected true — the member has one meaning and says it by being present
browserhive/storage-inventory.oversize-w: {where} carries both valuesOversize and unreadable — storage that could not be read has no size to have exceeded
{where} carries valuesOversize but storage.valuesRecorded is not true — no origin's values were going to be carried, so nothing was dropped at a bound
browserhive/storage-shape.areas-shape: line {line}: areas must contain local and session, each a JSON object
browserhive/storage-shape.declared-but-a: storage.valuesRecorded is true but {entry} is not in the package
browserhive/storage-shape.desc: browserhive: checks storage/origins.jsonl against the BrowserHive WACZ Profile, and against what the inventory says about it. A reader decides whether the archive carries stored values by reading valuesRecorded alone, so the two must agree.
browserhive/storage-shape.hidden-secret: {entry} is present, but the package has a hidden secret ({names}): a package with a hidden secret does not carry the stored values, which a page can have taken from a behavior
browserhive/storage-shape.not-json: {entry} line {line} is not a JSON object
browserhive/storage-shape.oversize-has-v: line {line}: {origin} is recorded as valuesOversize in the inventory but has values here — the inventory says they were too large to carry, and here they are
browserhive/storage-shape.present-but-un: {entry} is present but storage.valuesRecorded is not true
browserhive/storage-shape.unreadable-has: line {line}: {origin} is recorded as unreadable in the inventory but has values here
browserhive/tls-chain.bad-signature: {host}: certificate {index} is linked to the next one but its signature does not verify
browserhive/tls-chain.broken-link: {host}: certificate {index} does not link to the next one (issuer {issuer} vs subject {nextSubject})
browserhive/tls-chain.dangling-ref: {host}: chainRef {chainRef} points at no entry in tls.chains
browserhive/tls-chain.desc: browserhive: verifies the certificate chains in tls, using only what the package itself holds
browserhive/tls-chain.leaf-not-first: {host}: the first certificate does not cover this host (subject {subject}) — the leaf is not first
browserhive/tls-chain.unparseable: {host}: the chain behind {chainRef} could not be parsed as certificates
browserhive/tls-chain.verified: verified the certificate chain of {hosts} host(s)
browserhive/tls-san.desc: browserhive: checks the recorded san against the certificate the package carries
browserhive/tls-san.drift: {host}: san records {recorded} name(s) but the certificate carries {certificate}
browserhive/tls-san.host-not-covered: {host}: none of the recorded san names covers this host ({san})
browserhive/tls-san.missing: {host}: san is missing or is not an array of names
browserhive/url-policies.absent: settings.urlPolicies is missing. BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.3.0 requires it even when no request matched: an empty array is the claim that no policy was in force
browserhive/url-policies.bad-pattern: settings.urlPolicies has {count} entries whose pattern is not a string. A record of a withheld request names the pattern that matched, and a reader looks it up here
browserhive/url-policies.desc: browserhive: checks that the archive declares, in order, what the capture did about each URL pattern in force. BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.3.0 requires the list even when nothing matched, because an empty list is the claim that nothing was filtered; and it requires an action on each entry, because that is what says whether the request was sent at all.
browserhive/url-policies.not-array: settings.urlPolicies is {found}, expected an array of objects
browserhive/url-policies.unknown-action: settings.urlPolicies uses actions this version does not define: {found}. The action is what says whether the request was sent (deny) or sent but not kept (no-archive)
browserhive/policy-not-truncated.desc: browserhive: a body a policy omitted must not be listed as dropped at a size limit (completeness.truncatedUrls)
browserhive/policy-not-truncated.url-pol: {url} is listed in completeness.truncatedUrls, but the URL policy {pattern} (no-body) omitted its body — a body the capture never fetched cannot have reached a size limit
browserhive/policy-not-truncated.content: {url} is listed in completeness.truncatedUrls, but the content-type policy {prefix} omitted its body — a body the capture never fetched cannot have reached a size limit
browserhive/document-withheld.desc: browserhive: the page's text, its title and its accessibility tree are read from the rendered page, so a policy that kept the document's body out of the archive does not by itself keep them out. Checks browserhive:capture.document against the BrowserHive WACZ Profile (an archive that conforms to 1.10.0 is held to 1.10.0, where deny withholds nothing): withheld must be what the policies give for the document it names, in both directions; a withheld document leaves no text or title on its page entry (except an after-load snapshot's entry read from a document the policies do not withhold) and no accessibility tree; otherwise the tree names that document, not the requested URL
browserhive/document-withheld.not-object: browserhive:capture.document is {found}, expected a JSON object
browserhive/document-withheld.missing-ur: document has no url; only an unattributed document may leave it out
browserhive/document-withheld.unknown-re: document.withheld is {found}, which the version of the BrowserHive WACZ Profile the archive conforms to does not define (url-policy, content-type, no-archive, unattributed, and from 1.11.0 deny)
browserhive/document-withheld.should-wit: the policies give {expected} for the document {url}, but document.withheld is absent — its text, title and tree stayed in the archive although the policy kept its body out
browserhive/document-withheld.should-not: document.withheld is {declared}, but no policy applies to the document {url} — a policy that matched only a redirect hop or a document the page left withholds nothing
browserhive/document-withheld.wrong-reas: document.withheld is {declared}, but the policies give {expected} for the document {url}
browserhive/document-withheld.text-prese: the page entry has text although document.withheld is {withheld}
browserhive/document-withheld.title-pres: the page entry has a title although document.withheld is {withheld}
browserhive/document-withheld.axtree-pre: accessibility/axtree.jsonl is present although document.withheld is {withheld} — the tree carries the page's text
browserhive/document-withheld.text-withh: the page entry's textWithheld is {textWithheld}, but document.withheld is {withheld}
the page entry's textWithheld is {textWithheld}, but document.withheld is absent
browserhive/document-withheld.tree-url: line {line} of the accessibility tree names {treeUrl}, but the document it was read from is {url}
browserhive/document-withheld.not-in-arc: the document {url} is neither in the index, nor in a no-archive record (from BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.11.0, nor a deny record), nor in the document-uri of a snapshot or a screenshot — the archive holds no record of the document the page was read from
browserhive/deny-enforced.desc: browserhive: a deny policy promises that the request is never sent. Checks the WARC for request, response or revisit records of URLs whose first matching urlPolicies entry is deny; only a metadata record saying the request was withheld may stand for such a URL (BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.11.0)
browserhive/deny-enforced.sent: {url} has a {type} record although the first policy to match it, {pattern}, is deny — the request left the capturing machine
browserhive/window-shape.desc: browserhive: a record of a window not opened (a metadata record carrying window) says window: not-opened, names in WARC-Target-URI the URL the window would have loaded, names page or iframe in target when it has one, and carries no action — it is not a record of a withheld request (BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.12.0)
browserhive/window-shape.value: {url}: window is {value}, but the BrowserHive WACZ Profile defines only not-opened
browserhive/window-shape.uri: a window record (window: {value}) has no WARC-Target-URI — the URL the window would have loaded is what the record is for
browserhive/window-shape.target: {url}: target is {target}, but a window is asked for by a page or an iframe
browserhive/window-shape.action: {url}: a window record carries action {action} — it is not a record of a withheld request
browserhive/crashed-targets-listed.desc: browserhive: completeness.crashedTargets (targets other than the main document whose renderer crashed) is an array of well-formed entries, makes complete false when not empty, is sorted, and omits url when a policy or document.withheld says so (BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.21.0). Without this, an archive could deny that part of the page died during the capture.
browserhive/crashed-targets-listed.missi: completeness.crashedTargets is missing or not an array
browserhive/crashed-targets-listed.bad-e: completeness.crashedTargets[{index}]: type and status must be strings, and url, when present, a string
browserhive/crashed-targets-listed.compl: completeness.crashedTargets is not empty, but complete is true
browserhive/crashed-targets-listed.unsor: completeness.crashedTargets[{index}] is out of order: entries are sorted by url, type and status, with entries without a url first
browserhive/crashed-targets-listed.url-b: completeness.crashedTargets names {url}, but the first URL policy to match it is {action} ({pattern}); url must be omitted
completeness.crashedTargets names {url}, but document.withheld is {withheld}; url must be omitted
browserhive/unintercepted-listed.desc: browserhive: bodies that crossed the wire but could not be read as bytes (metadata truncated: not-intercepted) are listed in completeness.uninterceptedUrls, and their response records carry WARC-Truncated: unspecified (BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.13.0)
browserhive/unintercepted-listed.unliste: {url} has a record of a body not intercepted (truncated: not-intercepted) but is missing from completeness.uninterceptedUrls — the archive does not declare the missing body
browserhive/unintercepted-listed.unrecor: {url} is listed in completeness.uninterceptedUrls, but no record says truncated: not-intercepted for it
browserhive/unintercepted-listed.truncat: {url}: the response of a body not intercepted has WARC-Truncated {value}; it must be unspecified, or a reader of the WARC alone takes the empty payload for the body
browserhive/payload-charset.desc: browserhive: a text body that looks re-encoded by the writer rather than kept as the bytes the server sent (BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.13.0 forbids converting a body's character encoding; a guess, so a warning)
browserhive/payload-charset.transcoded: {url}: Content-Type declares charset={charset}, but the body does not decode as {charset} and does decode as UTF-8 — it looks rewritten to UTF-8
browserhive/payload-charset.double-encod: {url}: read as UTF-8 and turned back into windows-1252 bytes, the body decodes as UTF-8 again — it looks like a UTF-8 body read as windows-1252 and written back as UTF-8
browserhive/warc-files.desc: browserhive: archive/ holds only data-NNN.browserhive.warc.gz (data-NNN.warc.gz in an archive that declares BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.24.0 or earlier), numbered contiguously from 000; each file is compressed with GZIP (from WACZ Profile 1.25.0) and begins with a warcinfo that names it; every file but the last is at least settings.limits.maxWarcBytes long (WACZ Profile 1.14.0)
browserhive/warc-files.name: {entry} is not named {expected} — the archive directory holds only files of that name
browserhive/warc-files.not-gzip: {entry} is not compressed with GZIP (it does not begin with 1f 8b); from BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.25.0 every WARC file in archive/ is
browserhive/warc-files.gap: the WARC files are not numbered contiguously: expected {expected}, found {found}
browserhive/warc-files.first-record: {entry} does not begin with a warcinfo record (first record: {type})
browserhive/warc-files.filename: {entry}: its warcinfo names {found}; WARC-Filename must be the file's own name
browserhive/warc-files.under-limit: {entry} is {size} bytes, under maxWarcBytes {limit}, yet it is not the last file — a new file starts only once the current one reaches the limit
browserhive/warc-files.max-warc-bytes: settings.limits.maxWarcBytes is {found}; it must be a positive integer (bytes)
browserhive/wacz-name.desc: browserhive: an archive that declares BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.25.0 or later is named with a name that ends in .browserhive.wacz (a SHOULD; the mark is a hint, not a declaration of conformance). A name that cannot be told is not checked
browserhive/wacz-name.name: {name} does not end in .browserhive.wacz — from BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.25.0 the producer should name a BrowserHive WACZ so (the name does not decide conformance; conformsTo does)
browserhive/exchange-in-one-file.desc: browserhive: the response, request and metadata records of one exchange, and the resource and metadata records of one DOM snapshot or of one screenshot, are in the same WARC file (BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.14.0, BrowserHive WARC Profile 1.1.0 and 1.3.0)
browserhive/exchange-in-one-file.request: {url}: a record in {entry} is concurrent to a record in {other} — one exchange must not span files
browserhive/exchange-in-one-file.metadat: {url}: a metadata record in {entry} refers to a record in {other} — an exchange, a snapshot or a screenshot must not span files
browserhive/warcinfo-declares-profile.de: browserhive: each WARC file's warcinfo declares, in exactly one conformsTo field, the version of BrowserHive WARC Profile the file conforms to, and every file of the archive declares the same one (BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.16.0)
browserhive/warcinfo-declares-profile.mi: {entry}: its warcinfo has no conformsTo — from BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.16.0, each WARC file names the BrowserHive WARC Profile version it conforms to
browserhive/warcinfo-declares-profile.re: {entry}: its warcinfo has {count} conformsTo fields ({found}); it must have exactly one
browserhive/warcinfo-declares-profile.va: {entry}: its warcinfo conformsTo is {found}, which is not the URL of a BrowserHive WARC Profile version (https://uraitakahito.github.io/browserhive-warc-spec/N.N.N/)
browserhive/warcinfo-declares-profile.mi: {entry}: its warcinfo declares {found}, but {first} declares {expected} — every WARC file of one archive declares the same version
browserhive/snapshots.desc: browserhive: every DOM snapshot the capture took is the same one wherever it is read from — the snapshots member of datapackage, the resource and metadata records in the WARC, the page list and the index — and holds no script element (BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.17.0 and 1.18.0, BrowserHive WARC Profile 1.1.0)
browserhive/snapshots.shape: browserhive:capture.{at} in datapackage.json is {found} — from BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.17.0, snapshots is an array of one object per stage
browserhive/snapshots.stages: snapshots lists the stages {found}, but a capture with {behaviors} behaviors lists {expected} (exactly one after-load and, only when behaviors ran, one after-behaviors after it)
browserhive/snapshots.skipped: {stage}: the reason no snapshot was taken (skipped) is {found} — it must be withheld, too-large, task-budget or failed
browserhive/snapshots.url: {stage}: the url in snapshots is {url} — a snapshot URI begins with urn:browserhive:snapshot:{stage}:
browserhive/snapshots.no-resource: {stage}: the archive holds no resource record with the WARC-Record-ID <{record}> that snapshots names
browserhive/snapshots.mismatch: {stage} snapshot: {field} in {where} is {found}, but {otherField} in {other} is {expected}
browserhive/snapshots.no-metadata: {stage} snapshot ({url}): no WARC file holds a metadata record whose WARC-Refers-To names its resource record
browserhive/snapshots.script: {stage} snapshot ({url}) holds a script element — a snapshot holds none of the scripts of the page
browserhive/snapshots.unlisted: {url}: no entry of snapshots names this snapshot resource record (WARC-Record-ID {record})
browserhive/snapshots.pages: the page entries of pages/pages.jsonl have the stages {found} — they must be {expected}: from BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.18.0, the entry of the document (without stage) and then one entry per snapshot in the order of snapshots; in 1.17.0, one entry per snapshot in that order, or a single entry without stage when there is no snapshot
browserhive/snapshots.page-id: pages/pages.jsonl has more than one entry with the id {id} — readers keep only one of the entries that share an id
browserhive/snapshots.main-page: mainPageURL in datapackage.json is {found} — it is the url of the first entry of pages/pages.jsonl ({expected}): from BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.18.0 the entry of the document, in 1.17.0 the first snapshot when the package holds one
browserhive/snapshots.not-indexed: {stage} snapshot ({url}) has no line in indexes/index.cdxj — readers find a snapshot through the index
browserhive/snapshots.index-status: the index line of the {stage} snapshot ({url}) carries status {status} — a snapshot is not a response from a server, so its line carries no status
browserhive/screenshots.desc: browserhive: every screenshot the capture took at a stage is the same one wherever it is read from — the screenshots member of datapackage, the resource and metadata records in the WARC, and the index; the package of a capture that was asked to keep out what a picture could show (a secret, a media type policy, a withheld document, a no-archive or no-body policy that matched a request for a document, an image or media) holds none; and the picture is a still WebP image (BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.24.0, BrowserHive WARC Profile 1.3.0)
browserhive/screenshots.shape: browserhive:capture.{at} in datapackage.json is {found} — from BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.24.0, screenshots is an array of one object per stage
browserhive/screenshots.stages: screenshots lists the stages {found}, but a capture with {behaviors} behaviors lists {expected} (exactly one after-load and, only when behaviors ran, one after-behaviors after it)
browserhive/screenshots.skipped: {stage}: the reason the package holds no screenshot (skipped) is {found} — it must be disabled, secret, withheld, task-budget or failed
browserhive/screenshots.skipped-members: {stage}: an entry without a screenshot carries {members} — it carries stage and skipped, and nothing else
browserhive/screenshots.secret-without-s: {stage}: skipped is secret, but settings.secrets is empty — secret is the reason only when the capture was given a secret
browserhive/screenshots.skipped-not-secr: {stage}: skipped is {found}, but settings.secrets is not empty — in a capture that was given a secret every entry carries disabled or secret (where more than one reason holds, the first in the list is written)
browserhive/screenshots.skipped-not-with: {stage}: skipped is {found}, but a condition under which the package must hold no screenshot is true of it ({because}) — every entry carries disabled or withheld (where more than one reason holds, the first in the list is written)
browserhive/screenshots.missing-member: {stage}: an entry with a screenshot lacks {members} — it carries stage, url, date, record and bytes
browserhive/screenshots.url: {stage}: the url in screenshots is {url} — a screenshot URI begins with urn:browserhive:screenshot:{stage}:
browserhive/screenshots.no-resource: {stage}: the archive holds no resource record with the WARC-Record-ID <{record}> that screenshots names
browserhive/screenshots.mismatch: screenshot {shot}: {field} in {where} is {found}, but {otherField} in {other} is {expected}
browserhive/screenshots.unlisted: {url}: no entry of screenshots names this screenshot resource record (WARC-Record-ID {record})
browserhive/screenshots.snapshot-withhel: {stage}: snapshots records this stage as withheld, but its entry in screenshots carries no skipped — a package holds no screenshot of a stage whose document is withheld
browserhive/screenshots.forbidden-secret: the package holds a screenshot ({entries, plural, one {1 entry} other {# entries}} with a picture, {records, plural, one {1 resource record} other {# resource records}}), but settings.secrets is not empty — the package of a capture that was given a secret must hold no screenshot of any stage (a value cannot be replaced in a picture)
browserhive/screenshots.forbidden-conten: the package holds a screenshot ({entries, plural, one {1 entry} other {# entries}} with a picture, {records, plural, one {1 resource record} other {# resource records}}), but settings.contentTypePolicies is not empty — the package of a capture with a media type policy must hold no screenshot of any stage
browserhive/screenshots.forbidden-docume: the package holds a screenshot ({entries, plural, one {1 entry} other {# entries}} with a picture, {records, plural, one {1 resource record} other {# resource records}}), but document carries withheld ({withheld}) — a package whose document is withheld must hold no screenshot of any stage
browserhive/screenshots.forbidden-no-arc: the package holds a screenshot ({entries, plural, one {1 entry} other {# entries}} with a picture, {records, plural, one {1 resource record} other {# resource records}}), but a no-archive policy matched the request for {url} ({kind, select, typed {its resourceType is {resourceType}} other {its record carries no resourceType, so the package cannot show the kind of the request}}; {count, plural, one {1 such record} other {# such records}}) — a package of a capture in which a no-archive or no-body policy matched a request for a document, an image or media must hold no screenshot of any stage
browserhive/screenshots.forbidden-no-bod: the package holds a screenshot ({entries, plural, one {1 entry} other {# entries}} with a picture, {records, plural, one {1 resource record} other {# resource records}}), but a no-body policy matched the request for {url} ({kind, select, typed {the resourceType of its trace line is {resourceType}} untyped {the trace line that names its response carries no resourceType, so the package cannot show the kind of the request} other {no line of trace/events.jsonl names its response, so the package cannot show the kind of the request}}; {count, plural, one {1 such record} other {# such records}}) — a package of a capture in which a no-archive or no-body policy matched a request for a document, an image or media must hold no screenshot of any stage
browserhive/screenshots.resource-uri: {url}: the WARC-Target-URI of the screenshot is not in the defined form — urn:browserhive:screenshot:, the stage (after-load or after-behaviors), a colon, and the URL of the document at that stage
browserhive/screenshots.content-type: {url}: the Content-Type of the screenshot resource record is {found} — it must be image/webp
browserhive/screenshots.digest-missing: {url}: the screenshot resource record carries no {field}
browserhive/screenshots.digest: {url}: the {field} of the screenshot resource record is not the digest of its block
browserhive/screenshots.concurrent-to: {url}: the {type} record of the screenshot carries WARC-Concurrent-To — a screenshot is not part of an exchange
browserhive/screenshots.not-webp: {url}: the block cannot be read as a WebP image — one that begins with RIFF…WEBP, whose first chunk is VP8, VP8L or VP8X, and that is as long as it says
browserhive/screenshots.animated: {url}: the block is an animated WebP — a screenshot is a still image
browserhive/screenshots.no-metadata: {url}: no WARC file holds a metadata record whose WARC-Refers-To names the screenshot resource record
browserhive/screenshots.metadata-repeate: {url}: {count} metadata records name the screenshot resource record in WARC-Refers-To — there must be exactly one
browserhive/screenshots.metadata-orphan: {url}: the WARC-Refers-To ({refersTo}) of a metadata record that carries the screenshot field does not name a screenshot resource record
browserhive/screenshots.metadata-field-m: {url}: the metadata record of the screenshot lacks {fields} — it carries screenshot, document-uri, viewport, device-pixel-ratio and image-size
browserhive/screenshots.metadata-field-f: {url}: the metadata record of the screenshot carries {fields} — a reader would take it for a record of a withheld request, of a body not kept, of a window not opened, or of a snapshot
browserhive/screenshots.field-form: {url}: {field} in the metadata record of the screenshot is {found} — viewport and image-size are written like 1280x800 (decimal, 1 or more, no leading zero, a lowercase x), device-pixel-ratio in decimal, more than 0, with no zero that could be left out (2, 1.5)
browserhive/screenshots.image-size: {url}: image-size is {declared}, but the image in the block is {actual}
browserhive/screenshots.aspect: {url}: the image is {image} and the viewport is {viewport}, which differ in proportion by more than rounding to whole pixels — a screenshot shows the viewport and nothing beyond it
browserhive/screenshots.not-indexed: {url}: the screenshot has no line in indexes/index.cdxj — readers find the picture through the index
browserhive/screenshots.index-status: {url}: the index line of the screenshot carries status {status} — a picture is not a response from an origin, so its line carries no status
browserhive/redacted-records.desc: browserhive: a request or response record that says it had values replaced (BrowserHive-Redacted) has that field in its defined form and at least that many *** in the places it names. A record whose body was dropped for holding a hidden secret (WARC-Truncated: secret) holds no body and, if a response, is referred to by a metadata record with truncated: secret. Both describe the bytes they hold in their digests and HTTP Content-Length (BrowserHive WARC Profile 1.2.0). Passing does not mean the values are gone: wacz-validator does not know them, so a record that left a value in place, or replaced one without saying so, passes.
browserhive/redacted-records.type: a {type} record carries BrowserHive-Redacted ({url}): only request and response records may carry it
browserhive/redacted-records.repeated: {url}: BrowserHive-Redacted appears {count} times in one record
browserhive/redacted-records.form: {url}: BrowserHive-Redacted is "{found}": it lists target-uri, headers and payload in that order, each at most once, as name=count with a count of 1 or more and no leading zero, separated by a comma and a space
browserhive/redacted-records.count: {url}: BrowserHive-Redacted says {part}={declared}, but that place holds {found} ***
browserhive/redacted-records.truncated-n: {url}: this {type} record has WARC-Truncated: secret but holds no complete HTTP head: the producer records the message without its body, not without its head
browserhive/redacted-records.truncated-b: {url}: this {type} record has WARC-Truncated: secret but holds {bytes} bytes after the HTTP head: a dropped body is not in the record
browserhive/redacted-records.no-metadata: {url}: this response has WARC-Truncated: secret, but no metadata record with truncated: secret refers to it
browserhive/redacted-records.metadata-ta: {url}: a metadata record with truncated: secret refers to {target}, which is not a response with WARC-Truncated: secret
browserhive/redacted-records.digest: {url}: {field} does not describe the bytes the record holds: a digest of the bytes before replacement would let a reader test guesses of the value
browserhive/redacted-records.http-length: {url}: the HTTP Content-Length is {declared}, but the record holds a body of {actual} bytes
browserhive/logs-shape.desc: browserhive: logs/capture.jsonl, the log of the capture, is present, and each of its lines is a JSON object carrying the members BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.19.0 defines — profile browserhive:log/1, at as an RFC 3339 timestamp, ms as an integer of 0 or more that never falls below the line before, source and level from their fixed values, msg as a string; script on exactly the lines whose source is script, naming an entry of settings.behaviors; dpr, when present, one of settings.devicePixelRatios; truncated, when present, a boolean — and the log holds no line from the page when document carries withheld (WACZ Profile 1.19.0)
browserhive/logs-shape.missing: logs/capture.jsonl is absent — from BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.19.0 every package holds the log of its capture there, as an empty file when nothing was logged
browserhive/logs-shape.not-json: logs/capture.jsonl line {line} is not a JSON object — the log is JSON Lines, one object per line
browserhive/logs-shape.unknown-profile: logs/capture.jsonl line {line}: profile is {found} — a line of BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.19.0 carries browserhive:log/1
browserhive/logs-shape.missing-member: logs/capture.jsonl line {line} is missing {members} (required by BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.19.0)
browserhive/logs-shape.at: logs/capture.jsonl line {line}: at is {found}, which is not an RFC 3339 timestamp
browserhive/logs-shape.ms: logs/capture.jsonl line {line}: ms is {found} — it is an integer, 0 or more
browserhive/logs-shape.ms-decreased: logs/capture.jsonl line {line}: ms is {found}, less than the {previous} of line {previousLine} — the lines are in the order the producer received them, so ms never goes back
browserhive/logs-shape.source: logs/capture.jsonl line {line}: source is {found} — it must be script, page or browserhive
browserhive/logs-shape.level: logs/capture.jsonl line {line}: level is {found} — it must be debug, info, warn or error
browserhive/logs-shape.msg: logs/capture.jsonl line {line}: msg is {found}, which is not a string
browserhive/logs-shape.script-missing: logs/capture.jsonl line {line}: source is script, but the line has no script naming the behavior
browserhive/logs-shape.script-unexpected: logs/capture.jsonl line {line}: source is {source}, but the line carries script {found} — only a line whose source is script names a behavior
browserhive/logs-shape.script: logs/capture.jsonl line {line}: script is {found}, which is not the id of any entry of settings.behaviors ({behaviors})
browserhive/logs-shape.dpr: logs/capture.jsonl line {line}: dpr is {found}, which is not one of settings.devicePixelRatios ({ratios})
browserhive/logs-shape.truncated: logs/capture.jsonl line {line}: truncated is {found}, which is not a boolean
browserhive/logs-shape.withheld-page: document carries withheld ({withheld}), but logs/capture.jsonl holds {count, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}} whose source is page (the first at line {first}) — a package whose document is withheld holds no line from the page
browserhive/trace-shape.desc: browserhive: trace/events.jsonl, the trace of the capture, is present and declared in resources; browserhive:capture.trace says how many lines it holds; each line is a JSON object carrying the members BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.23.0 defines — profile browserhive:trace/1, kind request, id, hop, url, method, startedAt as an RFC 3339 timestamp, ms, and outcome from its fixed values; lines that share an id are in ascending order of hop; a line of a request that was not archived or was denied holds nothing of the answer; record, when present, names a response record in archive/ whose WARC-Date is the startedAt of the line; and when the trace left no line out, every http(s) response record is named by a line (WACZ Profile 1.23.0)
browserhive/trace-shape.summary-missing: browserhive:capture.trace is {found} — from BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.23.0 it is an object that says how many lines the trace holds (lines) and how many the producer left out (dropped)
browserhive/trace-shape.summary-member: browserhive:capture.trace.{member} is {found} — it is an integer, 0 or more
browserhive/trace-shape.line-count: browserhive:capture.trace.lines is {declared}, but trace/events.jsonl holds {found, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}}
browserhive/trace-shape.missing: trace/events.jsonl is missing — from BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.23.0 every package holds the trace of its capture there (an empty file when the trace has no lines)
browserhive/trace-shape.not-in-resources: trace/events.jsonl is not declared in the resources of datapackage.json — an entry left out of resources is covered by neither the digests of the package nor its signature
browserhive/trace-shape.not-json: trace/events.jsonl line {line} is not a JSON object — the trace is JSON Lines, one object per line
browserhive/trace-shape.unknown-profile: trace/events.jsonl line {line}: profile is {found} — a line of BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.23.0 declares browserhive:trace/1
browserhive/trace-shape.missing-member: trace/events.jsonl line {line} lacks {members} (required by BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.23.0)
browserhive/trace-shape.kind: trace/events.jsonl line {line}: kind is {found} — in BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.23.0 it is "request"
browserhive/trace-shape.outcome: trace/events.jsonl line {line}: outcome is {found} — it is one of finished, redirected, failed, pending, not-archived, denied and evicted
browserhive/trace-shape.not-string: trace/events.jsonl line {line}: {member} is {found} — it is a string
browserhive/trace-shape.hop: trace/events.jsonl line {line}: hop is {found} — it is an integer, 0 or more
browserhive/trace-shape.ms: trace/events.jsonl line {line}: ms is {found} — it is an integer, 0 or more
browserhive/trace-shape.started-at: trace/events.jsonl line {line}: startedAt is {found} — it is not an RFC 3339 timestamp
browserhive/trace-shape.hop-order: trace/events.jsonl line {line}: hop is {hop}, below the {previous} of line {previousLine}, which has the same id ({id}) — lines that share an id are in ascending order of hop
browserhive/trace-shape.hop-repeated: trace/events.jsonl line {line}: hop is {hop}, the same as line {firstLine}, which has the same id ({id}) — two lines of one redirect chain do not carry the same hop
browserhive/trace-shape.withheld-member: trace/events.jsonl line {line}: outcome is {outcome}, yet the line carries {members} — a line of a request that was not archived or was denied holds nothing of the answer, of what had the request made, or of a record
browserhive/trace-shape.error-missing: trace/events.jsonl line {line}: outcome is failed, yet the line has no error to say how the request failed
browserhive/trace-shape.error-unexpected: trace/events.jsonl line {line}: outcome is {outcome}, yet the line carries error — only a line whose outcome is failed does
browserhive/trace-shape.end-unobservable: trace/events.jsonl line {line}: outcome is {outcome}, yet the line carries endUnobservable — only a line whose outcome is pending does
browserhive/trace-shape.duration-unexpec: trace/events.jsonl line {line}: outcome is {outcome}, yet the line carries durationMs — only a line whose end the producer saw (finished, redirected or failed) does
browserhive/trace-shape.encoded-bytes-un: trace/events.jsonl line {line}: outcome is {outcome}, yet the line carries encodedBytes — only a line whose outcome is finished does
browserhive/trace-shape.flag-not-true: trace/events.jsonl line {line}: {member} is {found} — where it is present, its value is true
browserhive/trace-shape.data-url-not-cut: trace/events.jsonl line {line}: url is a data: URL, yet the line has no urlCut — a line does not hold the data of a data: URL, so its url is never the whole URL
browserhive/trace-shape.record-unknown: trace/events.jsonl line {line}: record is {found} — no response record in archive/ has that WARC-Record-ID
browserhive/trace-shape.started-at-diffe: trace/events.jsonl line {line}: startedAt is {found}, but the WARC-Date of the response record it names ({record}) is {date} — the two are the same, character for character
browserhive/trace-shape.record-repeated: trace/events.jsonl line {line}: record is {record}, which line {firstLine} already carries — two lines do not name the same record
browserhive/trace-shape.response-unnamed: {url}: no line of trace/events.jsonl names this response record ({record}), though browserhive:capture.trace.dropped is 0 — when the trace left no line out, every response record is named by the record of a line
browserhive/trace-shape.more: {message} (and {more, plural, one {1 more} other {# more}} like this in the same file)
browserhive/random-shape.desc: browserhive: browserhive:capture.random says whether the package holds the values the scripts of the captured page received at random — when recorded is true it carries documents, draws and truncated and no skipped, and the package holds random/values.jsonl and random/recorder.js, both declared in resources; when it is false it carries skipped (not-requested, withheld or failed) and the package holds neither entry, nor does a package whose document is withheld; each line is a JSON object with profile browserhive:random/1 and kind document or draw; document lines carry document (unique, ascending), url, frame (main or frame) and dpr, and record and date together, naming a response record in archive/ whose WARC-Date is date and whose WARC-Target-URI is url; draw lines carry document (of an earlier document line), seq (0, then one more per line of the document), api (Math.random, crypto.getRandomValues or crypto.randomUUID), caller, bytes for crypto.getRandomValues only, and value in the form its api sets; documents and draws are the numbers of those lines (WACZ Profile 1.26.0)
browserhive/random-shape.summary-missing: browserhive:capture.random is {found} — from BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.26.0 it is an object that says whether the package holds the values the page's scripts received at random (recorded), and how many lines hold them or why it holds none
browserhive/random-shape.recorded: browserhive:capture.random.recorded is {found} — it is true or false
browserhive/random-shape.summary-member: browserhive:capture.random.{member} is {found} — when recorded is true, documents and draws are integers, 0 or more, and truncated is true or false
browserhive/random-shape.summary-unexpec: browserhive:capture.random.recorded is {recorded}, yet random carries {members} — when recorded is true it carries no skipped, and when it is false it carries none of documents, draws and truncated
browserhive/random-shape.skipped: browserhive:capture.random.skipped is {found} — when recorded is false it is one of not-requested, withheld and failed
browserhive/random-shape.skipped-not-wit: browserhive:capture.random.skipped is failed, but document carries withheld ({withheld}) — where more than one reason holds, the first in the list (not-requested, withheld, failed) is written
browserhive/random-shape.skipped-withhel: browserhive:capture.random.skipped is withheld, but document carries no withheld — withheld says the document is withheld
browserhive/random-shape.count: browserhive:capture.random.{member} is {declared}, but random/values.jsonl holds {found, plural, one {# such line} other {# such lines}}
browserhive/random-shape.missing: {entry} is missing, though browserhive:capture.random.recorded is true — a package that holds the recorded values holds both random/values.jsonl and random/recorder.js (values.jsonl even when it has no draw line)
browserhive/random-shape.not-in-resource: {entry} is not declared in the resources of datapackage.json — an entry left out of resources is covered by neither the digests of the package nor its signature
browserhive/random-shape.unexpected: {entry} is in the package, though browserhive:capture.random.recorded is false — a package that holds no recorded values holds neither entry under random/
browserhive/random-shape.withheld-entry: {entry} is in the package, though document carries withheld ({withheld}) — the lines of random/values.jsonl are page-derived records, so a package whose document is withheld holds neither entry under random/
browserhive/random-shape.recorded-withhe: browserhive:capture.random.recorded is true, but document carries withheld ({withheld}) — a package whose document is withheld holds no entry under random/, so it holds no recorded values
browserhive/random-shape.not-json: random/values.jsonl line {line} is not a JSON object — the entry is JSON Lines, one object per line
browserhive/random-shape.unknown-profile: random/values.jsonl line {line}: profile is {found} — a line of BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.26.0 declares browserhive:random/1
browserhive/random-shape.missing-member: random/values.jsonl line {line} lacks {members} (required by BrowserHive WACZ Profile 1.26.0)
browserhive/random-shape.kind: random/values.jsonl line {line}: kind is {found} — it is "document" or "draw"
browserhive/random-shape.not-count: random/values.jsonl line {line}: {member} is {found} — it is an integer, 0 or more
browserhive/random-shape.not-string: random/values.jsonl line {line}: {member} is {found} — it is a string
browserhive/random-shape.document-repeat: random/values.jsonl line {line}: document is {document}, the same as the document line at line {firstLine} — two document lines do not carry the same document
browserhive/random-shape.document-order: random/values.jsonl line {line}: document is {document}, below the {previous} of the document line at line {previousLine} — document lines are in ascending order of document
browserhive/random-shape.frame: random/values.jsonl line {line}: frame is {found} — it is "main" or "frame"
browserhive/random-shape.dpr: random/values.jsonl line {line}: dpr is {found} — it is a number
browserhive/random-shape.record-date-pai: random/values.jsonl line {line} carries {present} but not {absent} — a document line carries record and date together, or neither
browserhive/random-shape.record-unknown: random/values.jsonl line {line}: record is {found} — no response record in archive/ has that WARC-Record-ID
browserhive/random-shape.date-differs: random/values.jsonl line {line}: date is {found}, but the WARC-Date of the response record it names ({record}) is {date} — the two are the same, character for character
browserhive/random-shape.url-differs: random/values.jsonl line {line}: url is {url}, but the WARC-Target-URI of the response record it names ({record}) is {target} — the two are the same, but for the values of kept secrets replaced in url
browserhive/random-shape.data-url-data: random/values.jsonl line {line}: url is a data: URL that holds its data — the line writes a data: URL up to and including its first comma, and nothing after it
browserhive/random-shape.draw-document-u: random/values.jsonl line {line}: document is {document}, which no earlier document line carries — the document of a draw line is that of a document line before it
browserhive/random-shape.seq-order: random/values.jsonl line {line}: seq is {seq}, but the draw line of document {document} here has {expected} — seq is 0 on the first draw line of a document and one more on each that follows
browserhive/random-shape.api: random/values.jsonl line {line}: api is {found} — it is one of Math.random, crypto.getRandomValues and crypto.randomUUID
browserhive/random-shape.bytes-missing: random/values.jsonl line {line}: api is crypto.getRandomValues, yet the line has no bytes
browserhive/random-shape.bytes-unexpecte: random/values.jsonl line {line}: api is {api}, yet the line carries bytes — only a line whose api is crypto.getRandomValues does
browserhive/random-shape.value: random/values.jsonl line {line}: value is {found}, which is not how a value of {api} is written — Math.random: a number, at least 0 and less than 1; crypto.randomUUID: 32 lowercase hexadecimal digits in groups of 8, 4, 4, 4 and 12; crypto.getRandomValues: base64 with the standard alphabet and padding (RFC 4648, section 4)
browserhive/random-shape.value-length: random/values.jsonl line {line}: value holds {found, plural, one {# byte} other {# bytes}}, but bytes is {bytes} — the value of crypto.getRandomValues is exactly bytes of them
browserhive/random-shape.more: {message} (and {more, plural, one {1 more} other {# more}} like this in the same file)
cdxj/filename-archive-relative.desc: indexes/index.cdxj entries must use archive-relative filenames (not "archive/...")
cdxj/filename-archive-relative.starts-wi: {entry} entry "filename" starts with "archive/" — wabac.js prepends archive/ itself, double-prefix breaks replay
cdxj/index-not-gzipped.desc: indexes/index.cdxj must not be gzipped (wabac.js silently ignores .cdxj.gz)
cdxj/index-not-gzipped.gzip-magic: {entry} starts with the gzip magic bytes — the file is named correctly but the content is compressed
cdxj/index-not-gzipped.gzipped-entry: Entry "{name}" is a gzipped CDXJ — wabac.js does not recognise .cdxj.gz / .cdx.gz
cdxj/index-recognised-by-wabac.desc: WACZ must contain a wabac-recognised index (.cdx / .cdxj / .idx)
cdxj/index-recognised-by-wabac.missing-p: {name} references "{pair}" but no such entry exists in the WACZ
cdxj/index-recognised-by-wabac.no-index: No wabac-recognised index file found under indexes/ — wabac.js needs at least one .cdx / .cdxj / .idx entry to serve any URL
cdxj/index-valid-data.desc: index CDXJ (plain or gzipped) must contain valid CDXJ data (WACZ 1.1.1 §5.2.2)
cdxj/index-valid-data.gzip-error: {entry} is named as gzipped but could not be decompressed (WACZ 1.1.1 §5.2.2: index files MUST contain CDXJ data)
cdxj/index-valid-data.invalid: {entry} line {line} is not valid CDXJ ({reason}) (WACZ 1.1.1 §5.2.2: index files MUST contain CDXJ data)
cdxj/pages-mainpage.desc: datapackage.mainPageURL must appear in both pages/pages.jsonl and indexes/index.cdxj
cdxj/pages-mainpage.no-cdxj-record: datapackage.json mainPageURL "{url}" has no record in indexes/index.cdxj
cdxj/pages-mainpage.not-in-pages: datapackage.json mainPageURL "{url}" is not listed in pages/pages.jsonl
cdxj/warc-offsets.desc: indexes/index.cdxj offset/length must land on a WARC gzip-member boundary
cdxj/warc-offsets.length-mismatch: indexes/index.cdxj line {line}: length {length} does not match WARC member at offset {offset} (actual {actual})
cdxj/warc-offsets.missing-or-nonnumeric: indexes/index.cdxj line {line}: offset / length missing or not numeric
cdxj/warc-offsets.offset-no-match: indexes/index.cdxj line {line}: offset {offset} does not match any WARC gzip-member start
cdxj/warc-offsets.file-not-in-archive: indexes/index.cdxj line {line}: filename {filename} names no file under archive/
datapackage/digest.absent: datapackage-digest.json is absent (WACZ 1.1.1 §5.2.5: SHOULD be included to verify datapackage.json)
datapackage/digest.desc: datapackage-digest.json should be present and its hash must match datapackage.json (WACZ 1.1.1 §5.2.5)
datapackage/digest.hash-mismatch: {entry} hash does not match the actual datapackage.json sha256
datapackage/frictionless-schema.desc: datapackage.json should conform to the Frictionless v1 schema (auxiliary)
datapackage/frictionless-structure.desc: datapackage.json must declare a non-empty resources array; each resource needs name and path (or data)
datapackage/frictionless-structure.no-re: datapackage.json has no resources (a non-empty resources array is required)
datapackage/profile-required.invalid-jso: {entry} is not valid JSON or not an object
datapackage/resource-hashes.desc: datapackage.json resource hashes must match the WACZ contents
datapackage/resource-hashes.invalid-path: {entry} resource is missing or has an invalid "path"
datapackage/resource-hashes.no-resources: {entry} has no "resources" array (or it is empty)
datapackage/resource-hashes.resource-mis: Resource "{path}" listed in {entry} is missing from the WACZ
datapackage/resources-complete.desc: every file in the WACZ must be listed in datapackage.json resources (WACZ 1.1.1 MUST)
datapackage/resources-complete.orphan: {entry} is not listed in datapackage.json resources (WACZ 1.1.1 MUST list all additional files)
datapackage/wacz-version-required.desc: datapackage.json must declare a non-empty wacz_version
i18n.smoke: {n, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} missing
report.more: {message} (and {more, plural, one {1 more} other {# more}} like this in the same file)
pages/page-schema.desc: each pages/pages.jsonl page line must be valid JSON with url and ts (WACZ 1.1.1 §5.2.3)
pages/page-schema.missing-prop: pages/pages.jsonl line {line} is missing required properties: {props}
pages/page-schema.not-json: pages/pages.jsonl line {line} is not valid JSON
wacz-auth/signature.cert-unparseable: signedData.domainCert is not a readable PEM certificate chain
wacz-auth/signature.desc: wacz-auth: checks that the signature in datapackage-digest.json covers the hash it claims, under the certificate the package carries, and that the certificate covers the domain it names. Uses only what the package holds — whether the chain reaches a trusted root, and whether the timestamp is valid, are the verifier's own decisions and are not asked here.
wacz-auth/signature.domain-mismatch: signedData.domainCert does not cover {domain} — the certificate that signed this archive is for a different name
wacz-auth/signature.signature-mismatch: signedData.signature does not verify against signedData.hash under the certificate in domainCert — the signature does not cover this archive
wacz-auth/signature.verified: signature verifies against the hash, under a certificate covering {domain} (chain trust and timestamp are not checked here)
wacz/file-extension.desc: the WACZ file's name ends in .wacz (WACZ 1.1.1 §Zip Format File Extension: a ZIP file that follows the WACZ format MUST use the extension .wacz); a name that cannot be told (an http URL whose last path segment has no dot) is not checked
wacz/file-extension.extension: {name} does not end in .wacz — WACZ 1.1.1 §Zip Format File Extension: a WACZ file MUST use the extension .wacz
wacz/required-files.desc: WACZ 1.1.1 §5.2 requires these files/directories to exist
wacz/required-files.missing-archive: archive/ has no WARC file (WACZ 1.1.1 §5.2.1: MUST contain at least one .warc/.warc.gz)
wacz/required-files.missing-datapackage: datapackage.json is missing (WACZ 1.1.1 §5.2.4: MUST exist at the root)
wacz/required-files.missing-indexes: indexes/ has no index file (WACZ 1.1.1 §5.2.2: MUST contain at least one .cdx/.cdxj/.idx)
wacz/required-files.missing-pages: pages/pages.jsonl is missing (WACZ 1.1.1 §5.2.3: MUST be present)
wacz/reserved-dirs-clean.desc: no custom files may be added to the reserved archive/ indexes/ pages/ directories (WACZ 1.1.1 MUST NOT)
wacz/reserved-dirs-clean.unexpected: {entry} is an unexpected file in the reserved "{dir}" directory (WACZ 1.1.1 MUST NOT add custom files there)
warc/extension-gzip-match.desc: archive WARCs must use .warc.gz when GZIP-encoded and .warc otherwise (WACZ 1.1.1 §5.2.1)
warc/extension-gzip-match.gz-needs-gz-ex: {entry} is GZIP-encoded but does not use the .warc.gz extension (WACZ 1.1.1 §5.2.1: GZIP WARCs MUST use .warc.gz)
warc/extension-gzip-match.plain-has-gz-e: {entry} uses the .warc.gz extension but its content is not GZIP-encoded
warc/members-independent.decode-failed: Failed to decode gzip member at offset {offset} (length {length})
warc/members-independent.desc: every WARC under archive/ must concatenate independent gzip members
warc/members-independent.no-members: {entry} contains no gzip members (empty or unrecognised)
warc/record-structure.desc: Every WARC record has the shape WARC 1.1 gives a record: a WARC/1.1 version line, name: value fields that end in CRLF, a blank line, a block of Content-Length bytes and a closing CRLF CRLF
warc/record-structure.no-version-line: WARC record #{record} does not start with a WARC version line (found "{found}") — it is not read as a record
warc/record-structure.version-not-1-1: WARC record #{record} declares {found}, not WARC/1.1 — it is checked against the WARC 1.1 rules anyway
warc/record-structure.lf-line-ending: WARC record #{record}: header lines end in LF instead of CRLF
warc/record-structure.no-blank-line: WARC record #{record}: no blank line separates the header from the block — it is not read as a record
warc/record-structure.bad-field-line: WARC record #{record}, header line {line}: "{found}" is not a name: value field
warc/record-structure.folded-line: WARC record #{record}, header line {line}: the value of {found} is folded onto a continuation line
warc/record-structure.non-utf8: WARC record #{record}: the header is not valid UTF-8
warc/record-structure.content-length-mis: WARC record #{record} has no Content-Length, so the end of its block cannot be found
warc/record-structure.content-length-for: WARC record #{record}: Content-Length "{found}" is not a number of bytes
warc/record-structure.content-length-mis: WARC record #{record}: Content-Length says {declared} bytes but the block has {actual}
warc/record-structure.no-terminator: WARC record #{record}: the block is not followed by the CRLF CRLF that ends a record
warc/record-structure.first-record-not-w: the file starts with a {type} record — WARC 1.1 recommends starting each file with a warcinfo record
warc/mandatory-fields.desc: WARC records carry the fields WARC 1.1 makes mandatory: WARC-Record-ID, WARC-Date and WARC-Type on every record, and WARC-Target-URI, WARC-Profile and the segment fields where the record type needs them
warc/mandatory-fields.missing: WARC record #{record} has no {field}, which every record must have
warc/mandatory-fields.missing-for-type: WARC record #{record} ({type}) has no {field}, which a {type} record must have
warc/fields-by-type.desc: WARC records carry only the fields WARC 1.1 allows for their type, and no defined field twice (WARC-Concurrent-To excepted)
warc/fields-by-type.forbidden: WARC record #{record} ({type}) has {field}, which a {type} record must not carry
warc/fields-by-type.repeated: WARC record #{record} has {field} {count} times — it may appear only once
warc/fields-by-type.undefined-field: WARC record #{record} ({type}) has {field}, which WARC 1.1 does not define for {type} records
warc/field-values.desc: The values of the WARC 1.1 fields have the form the standard gives them: record IDs in angle brackets, bare URIs, W3CDTF timestamps in UTC, numbers, labelled digests, IP addresses and media types
warc/field-values.record-id-form: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is not a URI in angle brackets
warc/field-values.uri-angle-brackets: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is wrapped in angle brackets, which WARC 1.1 dropped from this field
warc/field-values.uri-form: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is not an absolute URI
warc/field-values.date-form: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is not a W3CDTF timestamp
warc/field-values.date-fraction-digits: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" has more than 9 digits of fractional seconds
warc/field-values.date-not-utc: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is not in UTC
warc/field-values.digits-form: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is not a decimal number
warc/field-values.digest-form: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is not of the form algorithm:value
warc/field-values.ip-brackets: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is wrapped in brackets — an IPv6 address is written bare
warc/field-values.ip-form: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is neither a dotted-quad IPv4 nor an IPv6 address
warc/field-values.media-type-form: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is not a media type (type/subtype with optional parameters)
warc/field-values.digest-label-uppercase: WARC record #{record}: {field} uses the label "{label}" — labels are recommended in lowercase
warc/field-values.ip-not-canonical: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is not in the canonical IPv6 form ({canonical})
warc/field-values.unknown-record-type: WARC record #{record} has the type "{value}", which WARC 1.1 does not define — readers ignore such records
warc/field-values.unknown-truncated-reas: WARC record #{record}: {field} "{value}" is not one of length, time, disconnect and unspecified
warc/content-type.desc: WARC records carry the Content-Type WARC 1.1 recommends: one on every non-empty block, application/http on HTTP requests and responses, application/warc-fields on warcinfo
warc/content-type.missing: WARC record #{record} ({type}) has a block but no Content-Type
warc/content-type.not-application-http: WARC record #{record} ({type}) of an HTTP URI has Content-Type "{value}" instead of application/http
warc/content-type.msgtype-mismatch: WARC record #{record} ({type}) says msgtype={msgtype} in its Content-Type
warc/content-type.warcinfo-not-warc-fiel: WARC record #{record} (warcinfo) has Content-Type "{value}" — application/warc-fields is recommended
warc/revisit.desc: revisit records follow their WARC-Profile: one of the two WARC 1.1 profiles, a WARC-Payload-Digest and WARC-Truncated: length for identical-payload-digest, and the recommended WARC-Refers-To fields
warc/revisit.unknown-profile: WARC record #{record} (revisit) names the profile {value}, which WARC 1.1 does not define — readers do not interpret its block
warc/revisit.profile-uri-1-0: WARC record #{record} (revisit) is WARC/1.1 but names the WARC 1.0 profile {value}
warc/revisit.digest-missing: WARC record #{record} (revisit, identical-payload-digest) has no WARC-Payload-Digest
warc/revisit.truncated-missing: WARC record #{record} (revisit, identical-payload-digest) keeps a block but has no WARC-Truncated: length
warc/revisit.truncated-not-length: WARC record #{record} (revisit, identical-payload-digest) keeps a block with WARC-Truncated "{found}" — the reason must be length
warc/segmentation.desc: Segmented records form a proper series: an origin numbered 1, continuations numbered from 2 without gaps, one target URI, and a WARC-Segment-Total-Length on the last continuation that matches the blocks
warc/segmentation.origin-number: WARC record #{record} starts a segmented series but has WARC-Segment-Number {found}, not 1
warc/segmentation.origin-is-continuation: WARC record #{record} names {origin} as its origin, which is itself a continuation
warc/segmentation.number-sequence: WARC record #{record}: the continuations of this series are numbered {found} — they must count up from 2 by one
warc/segmentation.target-uri-differs: WARC record #{record} (continuation) has WARC-Target-URI {found}, but its series has {expected}
warc/segmentation.total-length-missing: WARC record #{record} is the last continuation of its series but has no WARC-Segment-Total-Length
warc/segmentation.total-length-not-last: WARC record #{record} has WARC-Segment-Total-Length but is not the last continuation of its series
warc/segmentation.total-length-mismatch: WARC record #{record}: WARC-Segment-Total-Length says {declared} bytes but the blocks of the series add up to {actual}
warc/segmentation.origin-not-found: WARC record #{record} (continuation) points to the origin {origin}, which is not in this WACZ
warc/segmentation.no-continuation: WARC record #{record} starts a segmented series, but none of its continuations is in this WACZ
warc/segmentation.extra-fields: WARC record #{record} (continuation) carries {fields} — segments after the first should carry only what continues the record
warc/payload-digest.desc: WARC records' WARC-Payload-Digest must match a fresh sha256 of the payload
warc/payload-digest.no-http-body: WARC record #{memberIdx} ({recordType}) has WARC-Payload-Digest but no parseable HTTP body
warc/payload-digest.non-sha256: WARC record #{memberIdx} uses non-sha256 digest "{algo}" — not verified
warc/recording-complete.desc: browserhive: surface how many recorded requests were incomplete/failed (metadata records of a BrowserHive WARC file)
warc/recording-complete.incomplete: {incomplete} of {total} recorded requests are incomplete or failed ({percent}%)
warc/storage-store.desc: every WARC under archive/ must be stored with method STORE (0), not DEFLATE
warc/storage-store.zip-compressed: {entry} is zip-compressed (method {method}) — should be STORE (0) so CDXJ offsets seek correctly
